newsitem.title: FRANCE: Four sentenced in French Alps cable-car collapse.
newsitem.headline: Four sentenced in French Alps cable-car collapse.

text.p: A French court on Monday gave suspended jail sentences to four company officials blamed for the collapse of a cable-car in the French Alps in 1989 that killed eight technicians testing the vehicle.

The Grenoble court handed Jean-Pierre Cathiard, chairman of the Pomagalski company, the world's biggest manufacturer of such equipment, an 18-month suspended sentence. He was also fined 30,000 francs ($6,000).
Cathiard's technical director Serge Tarassof was given an identical sentence. All those convicted were found guilty of manslaughter.

Two other officials were given 18- and 16-month suspended jail terms for the January 1989 accident in Vaujany in which the cable-car plunged 200 metres (yards) to the ground during tests a week before it was due to go into service.
